prompt: Write IntMatrix.java, a class that owns a 2D int array and only ever hands out copies, then write the static add, transpose, columnMaxima and isSymmetric operations in MatrixOps.java.
explanation: A 2D array in Java is an array of row arrays, so cells[r][c] means row r, column c and cells.length is the row count while cells[0].length is the column count. Returning a copy from row() and toArray() protects the matrix: handing back the real array would let a caller change cells behind the class's back. transpose swaps the roles of the indexes -- result.set(c, r, m.get(r, c)) -- which is also why the new matrix has the dimensions the other way round.
hints: Inside IntMatrix, cols() must cope with a matrix that has no rows at all, since cells[0] would not exist.
row() should allocate a new int[cols()] and copy the values across one at a time.
For isSymmetric, first reject anything that is not square, then compare get(r, c) with get(c, r) for every pair.
